label: CATALOGUE
note: CATALOGUE marks a data file of research statuses and references; it is not a result label.

mechanisms.name: Five-layer diffusion, constant diffusivity per layer
mechanisms.status_basis: STRATO v1.0 solves the layered equation by finite volume (Code B) and by an eigenfunction series (Code C); the tests show second-order convergence in space, first-order convergence in time, a balance residual at round-off level and agreement of the two codes on the synthetic five-layer case. Verification only: no comparison with measurements exists.
mechanisms.missing_work: A comparison with measured release needs temperature-dependent diffusivity (web phase 6.2) and the validation of web phase 7.

species.summary: Ag-110m, an activation product with a 249.83 d half-life, passes through intact SiC coatings; AGR-1 compacts released from about 0 % to more than 90 % of it.
Palladium has no isotope of radiological consequence but crosses intact SiC and corrodes it, a key contributor to the SiC failures found in AGR-1 particles.
Caesium is effectively retained by intact SiC, so its release measures SiC integrity; Cs-137 is one of the owner's first Phase 2 nuclides.
Strontium passes intact coatings in small amounts and is held in the OPyC and matrix; Sr-90 is one of the owner's first Phase 2 nuclides.
Europium passes intact coatings at levels about ten times those of strontium and is largely held in the OPyC and compact matrix.
Radioiodine is expected to be released like the fission gases through failed coatings; deferred in STRATO because no PyC or SiC iodine diffusivity is registered.
Ruthenium, a noble-metal fission product, was retained even in AGR-1 particles with failed SiC; little transport evidence exists.
Xenon is a fission gas held gas-tight by intact SiC; its release-to-birth ratio monitored AGR-1 for coating failures.
Krypton release indicates TRISO coating failure; Kr-85 is the owner's second Phase 2 nuclide, with a precursor-delay caveat.

references.citation: Morris, R. N., Baldwin, C. A., Demkowicz, P. A., Hunn, J. D., & Reber, E. L. (2016). Performance of AGR-1 high-temperature reactor fuel during post-irradiation heating tests. Nuclear Engineering and Design, 306, 24-35. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nucengdes.2016.04.031
references.notes: Accepted manuscript (OSTI 1325505) read. AGR-1 safety tests at 1600-1800 °C on 14 compacts: Cs release below 5e-6 with intact SiC; SiC failures about 3 of 33,100 (1600 °C), 4 of 8300 (1700 °C), 23 of 16,500 (1800 °C); Kr-85 below 5e-6 except two TRISO failures at 1800 °C; Eu and Sr release dominated by OPyC and matrix inventory; HRB-15B results as reported. Source of register measurement rows.

references.citation: Collin, B. P., Petti, D. A., Demkowicz, P. A., & Maki, J. T. (2015). Comparison of silver, cesium, and strontium release predictions using PARFUME with results from the AGR-1 irradiation experiment. Journal of Nuclear Materials, 466, 426-442. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2015.08.033
references.notes: Accepted manuscript opened; abstract, introduction and Section 5 headings read. PARFUME over-predicted Cs release (factor up to 3 failed SiC, up to 100 intact; diffusivity in UCO up to 250 times and in SiC about 40 % too high) and Sr release from intact particles; intact and failed particles modelled separately and combined per compact.

references.citation: Collin, B. P., Petti, D. A., Demkowicz, P. A., & Maki, J. T. (2016). Comparison of fission product release predictions using PARFUME with results from the AGR-1 safety tests. Nuclear Engineering and Design, 301, 378-390. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nucengdes.2016.03.023
references.notes: Accepted manuscript (INL/JOU-15-34147) abstract read. PARFUME over-predicted safety-test release of Ag, Sr and Kr, and of Cs from intact particles (up to five orders of magnitude); tentative correction factors for Ag and Cs only. Its Table 2 diffusivities are register rows C16-01 to C16-23. Correction factors are never STRATO defaults (owner decision D4).

references.citation: Scates, D., Walter, J., Drigert, M., Reber, E., & Harp, J. (2010). Fission product monitoring and release data for the Advanced Gas Reactor-1 experiment (INL/CON-10-17996; preprint, HTR 2010, Paper 52). Idaho National Laboratory.
references.notes: Preprint read. AGR-1 fission product monitoring system: Kr and Xe isotopes in the sweep gas, release-to-birth ratios, Kr-85m R/B mostly below 1e-7; I-135 from Xe-135m after shutdown; eq. 6 (failure plus contamination); Booth equivalent-sphere model; release attributed to uranium contamination.

references.citation: Compere, E. L., Kirslis, S. S., Bohlmann, E. G., Blankenship, F. F., & Grimes, W. R. (1975). Fission product behavior in the Molten Salt Reactor Experiment (ORNL-4865). Oak Ridge National Laboratory. https://doi.org/10.2172/4077644
references.notes: Report opened; abstract (printed p. 1) and introduction (p. 2) read. Fuel dissolved in a circulating fluoride salt (not TRISO particles in a coolant): Kr and Xe stripped to the off-gas; Rb, Cs, Sr, Ba, Y, Zr and lanthanides stayed in the salt; iodine indicated to stay in the salt; noble metals Nb, Mo, Tc, Ru, Ag, Sb, Te deposited on surfaces. The author order differs between the cover (used here) and the title page.

gallery.title: Cubic SiC reference cell
gallery.caption: Planned reference cell of cubic (3C) SiC for later defect and boundary models. The AGR-1 SiC is cubic but polycrystalline and heavily faulted; an ideal crystal does not represent the coating. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of the repeating atomic unit of perfect cubic silicon carbide, used only as a starting point; the real coating is made of many small, faulted grains. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: crystal building and periodic density-functional relaxation in BIOVIA Materials Studio (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Σ3 grain boundary in 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned bicrystal of a Σ3 twin boundary, a boundary type present in high fraction in the AGR-1 SiC. Σ3 boundaries cannot give a connected path through the layer and bound boundary diffusion from below. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of two SiC grains meeting at a highly ordered type of boundary that is frequent in the AGR-1 coating. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: bicrystal built in Materials Studio, pre-relaxed with an empirical potential (Forcite module), then density-functional relaxation (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Σ5 grain boundary in 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned Σ5 (210)/[001] boundary, for which faster Ag diffusion than in random high-angle boundaries has been reported, and where Ag and Pd diffusion have been simulated atomistically. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of a less ordered boundary between two SiC grains, a candidate fast path for silver. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: as for the Σ3 boundary (Forcite pre-relaxation, CASTEP relaxation).

gallery.title: High-energy (random) grain boundary
gallery.caption: Planned model of a high-energy boundary region, represented in the literature as amorphous SiC, which is expected to provide percolating fast paths. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of a disordered boundary region between SiC grains, the kind expected to connect across the coating. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: melt-quench molecular dynamics with an empirical potential (Forcite module) to build the disordered region, then density-functional relaxation of a smaller cell.
gallery.conditions: Planned: quench and relaxation; finite-temperature runs within the AGR-1 range of time-average, volume-average compact temperatures (955 to 1136 °C, demkowicz2016).

gallery.title: Vacancies and interstitials in 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned set of intrinsic point defects (carbon and silicon vacancies, interstitials, antisites), the defects that irradiation multiplies and that bind silver. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of missing and extra atoms in the SiC crystal, the kind of damage that radiation creates. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional defect formation energies in a supercell (CASTEP module).
gallery.conditions: Planned: static relaxation at 0 K; charge states to be chosen from the literature.

gallery.title: Silver impurity configurations in bulk 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned silver on silicon and carbon sites, as an interstitial, and bound to vacancies; the literature finds Ag on a silicon site bound to a carbon vacancy most stable in the bulk. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of single silver atoms sitting in different places inside a perfect SiC crystal. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional formation and binding energies (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Silver segregation to a grain boundary
gallery.caption: Planned silver sites in a Σ3 boundary compared with the bulk; the literature reports formation energies 2 to 4 eV lower in the boundary. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of silver atoms preferring to sit in the boundary between two grains rather than inside a grain. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional energies of Ag at boundary and bulk sites (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Silver migration pathway along a grain boundary
gallery.caption: Planned minimum-energy path for a silver hop along a boundary. Any barrier from it is an atomistic migration barrier and is not converted on the page into an effective diffusivity of the coating. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of the route a silver atom takes when it jumps from one site to the next along a boundary, with the energy hill it has to climb. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: transition-state search (nudged elastic band) on density-functional energies (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Silver at a pore surface (trapping site)
gallery.caption: Planned silver adsorption and desorption at a SiC surface representing a nano-pore wall; desorption-limited pores are proposed as reversible traps. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of a silver atom stuck to the wall of a tiny pore in the coating, a place where it could be held for a while. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional adsorption energies and desorption path (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Silver at a triple junction
gallery.caption: Planned silver at the junction of three grains, where silver precipitates were observed in irradiated AGR-1 SiC and which may act as traps. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of silver at a point where three grains of the coating meet. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: empirical-potential construction (Forcite module) and density-functional energies of Ag sites in a reduced cell (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Palladium interaction with a SiC surface
gallery.caption: Planned palladium atoms on a SiC surface; ab initio molecular dynamics in the literature shows palladium disintegrating the surface and removing carbon. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of palladium atoms attacking the surface of silicon carbide. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: ab initio molecular dynamics (CASTEP module).
gallery.conditions: Planned: finite temperature within the AGR-1 range of time-average, volume-average compact temperatures (955 to 1136 °C, demkowicz2016); higher temperatures only if justified by a source.

gallery.title: Palladium at Σ3 and Σ5 grain boundaries
gallery.caption: Planned palladium sites and paths at Σ3 and Σ5 boundaries, where atomistic palladium diffusion far faster than observed nodule penetration has been reported. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of palladium atoms in the boundaries between SiC grains. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional energies and migration paths (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Palladium and silver at the same boundary site
gallery.caption: Planned co-location of palladium and silver at a boundary or triple junction, as observed in some precipitates of irradiated AGR-1 SiC. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of a silver atom and a palladium atom side by side in a grain boundary, to test whether palladium helps silver move. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional binding energies of Ag-Pd pairs at boundary sites (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Palladium silicide at a SiC grain boundary
gallery.caption: Planned palladium silicide in contact with SiC, the reaction product reported for palladium attack; precipitates of Pd, U and Si were found in AGR-1 SiC. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of the compound that forms when palladium reacts with silicon carbide. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: interface construction and density-functional relaxation (CASTEP module); silicide phase to be taken from a cited source.

gallery.title: Caesium in bulk 3C-SiC and at a grain boundary
gallery.caption: Planned caesium sites in the bulk and at a grain boundary of 3C-SiC. Caesium is effectively retained by intact SiC; published atomistic boundary diffusion coefficients for caesium are far slower than experiment, so any result would be compared with that disagreement, not converted into an effective diffusivity. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of single caesium atoms inside silicon carbide and in the boundary between two grains, the layer that holds caesium back. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional formation and binding energies (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Strontium and europium in 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned strontium and europium configurations in 3C-SiC and at a grain boundary. Both elements passed intact AGR-1 coatings in small amounts and were held in the outer pyrocarbon and matrix. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of strontium and europium atoms inside silicon carbide, two elements that leak slowly through intact coatings. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional formation energies of substitutional and interstitial sites (CASTEP module).

gallery.title: Krypton, xenon and iodine at vacancies in 3C-SiC
gallery.caption: Planned krypton, xenon and iodine atoms at vacancy sites and small cavities of 3C-SiC. An intact SiC layer keeps the particle gas-tight; the calculation would examine where these atoms sit, not predict a release. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.alt_text: A planned picture of large krypton, xenon and iodine atoms trapped in gaps of the silicon carbide crystal, the layer that keeps fission gases inside the particle. This calculation has not been performed. It is planned for a future phase of the project.
gallery.method: Planned: density-functional incorporation energies at vacancy sites (CASTEP module).
